text: Our office espresso machine is leaking. A wants a simpler one and B wants to keep the old one. I don't want a fight over coffee. Can you help us sort it out?

Happy to help sort this out calmly. To keep things organized, I will keep a shared list of everyone's concerns and proposed options. First, could you tell me your own main concerns about the machine and grinder? Also, do you know what is wrong with the current machine, and whether anyone has looked at repair options?

My main concern is just getting coffee working again without this turning into a bigger disagreement. The machine is leaking; I don’t know whether anyone has looked into repairs, and I can’t take on coordinating that. I’d want any replacement to work with the grinder.

Hello A, C has asked me to help everyone sort out the office espresso machine situation. I understand you would prefer a simpler machine. Could you briefly share your main concerns with the current one, and what you would like to see instead? I will keep a shared list of everyone's concerns so we can find a fair plan.

Thanks for coordinating. The leak and upkeep are my main concerns, and I’m afraid I can’t take on repairs or a cleaning rota. I’d favor a simpler, low-maintenance machine, while recognizing the old one means a lot to B.

Hello B, C has asked me to help everyone sort out the office espresso machine situation. I understand you would like to keep the current machine. Could you briefly share why, and any concerns you have about replacing it? I will keep a shared list of everyone's concerns so we can find a fair plan.

I want it repaired and kept—it was my late father’s, and it means a lot to me. But it keeps breaking, and I don’t have much time for repairs or long discussions. I know A wants something simpler; I’m not sure what C wants.

Thank you for sharing, B. Since the machine belonged to your late father, here is one idea: it could be professionally repaired and kept by you at home, where you can enjoy it without the wear of office use. The office would then get a simpler, low-maintenance machine that suits A and works with the grinder. Would something like that work for you?

No. I want it kept in the office, not turned into something I have to manage at home. I want it repaired, but it can’t become another ongoing job for me. Any discussion needs to fit into a short slot.

Quick update: B has explained the machine belonged to her late father, so she wants it repaired and kept in the office. She also cannot take on repair coordination herself. Could you live with keeping the current machine if it is professionally repaired and its day-to-day upkeep is shared among the three of you in a simple way? Or would a simpler machine still be your strong preference?
I understand why B wants to keep it, but even simple shared upkeep would be hard for me to take on. I’d still prefer a low-maintenance machine.

Thank you, that is clear. Here is a possible plan I will check with the others: the machine is repaired by a professional, and upkeep after that is split simply among the three of you, so it does not fall on any one person, and no one has to coordinate a big project. Discussions happen in one short slot. Does that sound acceptable in principle?
In principle, yes—if the upkeep is genuinely shared and doesn’t turn into a regular job for me. The details of the split still need deciding. A short discussion works.

Thanks for the honest answer. New idea to test: the machine stays and is repaired, and instead of anyone doing regular upkeep, a professional services it on a schedule (for example, twice a year). Nobody takes on a cleaning rota or repair coordination. Would that remove your objection to keeping the current machine?
That would ease my main concern, provided the leak is fixed and the service really requires no ongoing effort from us. I’d still prefer a simpler machine, but I could live with this arrangement.

Quick update: A says even shared upkeep would be hard for her, so I am testing a version where nobody has ongoing chores: a professional services the machine on a fixed schedule, and no one coordinates repairs or keeps a cleaning rota. I will let you know how A responds. If that works for everyone, the remaining detail is simply agreeing the service arrangement in your short discussion.
That sounds better, as long as the cost and schedule are agreed first. I’m open to a short discussion, but I haven’t agreed to an arrangement yet.

Good news: A and B are both open to a plan to keep the current machine. The idea is: a professional repairs the leak, then services the machine on a fixed schedule (for example, twice a year), so nobody has a cleaning rota or repair job. B wants the cost and schedule agreed first. A can live with this even though she would still prefer a simpler machine. As the person who does not want to coordinate this, would you be willing for the three of you to hold one short discussion to agree the cost and service schedule? That would close out all the open points.
Yes, I’m willing to join one short discussion to agree the cost and schedule, as long as someone else sets it up.

Small update: C will join the short discussion to agree the cost and schedule, but asks that someone else handles setup. Could you be the one to arrange the discussion and make the single booking call once the details are agreed? It would be a one-time task, not an ongoing job, and it would keep the machine in the office as you want.
No, I can’t take on arranging it or making the call. I can join a short discussion if it fits my schedule.

We are nearly there. The plan taking shape: the current machine stays, a professional repairs the leak and then services it on a fixed schedule, so nobody has an ongoing cleaning rota or repair job. B and C will join one short discussion to agree cost and schedule, but both say they cannot set it up or make the booking call. Would you be willing to arrange the short discussion and make the one-time booking call, even though you prefer a simpler machine? That one-time task would be the whole of your effort under this plan.
I’m sorry, but I can’t take on arranging the discussion or making the booking call. I can join the short discussion.

A and B will both join the short discussion, but neither can set it up or make the booking call. Since you started this process and want coffee working again, would you be willing to take one small piece: send a short email to one or two local repairers asking for a quote for fixing the leak and a service price? That is a single email, not coordination. Then the three of you can pick in your short discussion, and whoever is easiest that day makes the booking call.
I’m sorry, I can’t take on contacting repairers. I can join the discussion once someone has quotes.

Update: none of the three of you can take on setup tasks beforehand. So here is a simpler proposal. The three of you hold one short discussion, ideally over a coffee break. In that meeting you would: agree whether to repair the current machine with professional servicing or buy a simpler machine, look at one or two options on your phones together, agree the cost, and decide on the spot who makes the call or order. Deciding who acts in the moment is much easier than assigning it in advance. Would you be willing to join that one short meeting on those terms?
Yes, I can join one short meeting on those terms. I’d still favor a simpler machine, and I can’t take on ongoing upkeep.
